newsitem.title: INDIA: India denies Kashmir rights abuses allegations.
newsitem.headline: India denies Kashmir rights abuses allegations.

text.p: India said on Wednesday that allegations by Kashmiri separatists of increasing human rights abuses by security forces were misleading and ridiculous.

"Surprisingly, they (All Parties Hurriyat Conference) are whipping the human rights issue when the actual number of complaints received by the government is showing a marked decline," a government statement said.
"Hurriyat propaganda is ridiculous," the statement said.

The All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, an umbrella organisation of more than 30 separatist groups, last week said human rights violations by soldiers deployed in Kashmir to fight a seven-year-old revolt had increased in recent months.
The government statement said: "More than 5,800 innocent civilians were killed by the militants since 1990. The Hurriyat and its other associates should make their position clear on these killings.
"It is intriguing that the Hurriyat is trying to cover up human rights violations on one hand and crying itself hoarse on this subject to mislead the people," it said.
The government said it was not protecting anyone, and noted at least 224 army and paramilitary personnel had been punished for rights violations since the rebellion broke out in 1990.
"Even the army and security forces are made accountable for their actions, and punishments range from dismissal from the services to reduction in the ranks," the statement said.
"In the last five years, the government has investigated 2,600 cases of alleged human rights violations, of which 2,288 were found false after the investigation," it said.

Dozens of guerrilla groups have been fighting since 1990 for the Himalayan region's independence or merger with neighbouring Pakistan. Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have died in insurgency-related violence.
